**What is Finary?**

We are on a mission to **give power back to investors**. Great financial guidance has always existed, it just came with a minimum net worth. We're changing that by building the AI-powered one-stop shop for investing, where you can track your assets, manage your budget, invest, and learn. One simple, ambitious idea drives us: put a private banker in everyone's pocket.

[Mounir](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mounirlaggoune/) launched Finary in 2021, and more than 1,000,000 people now trust us with their financial lives. We ship cutting-edge products with touches of delight, and we care deeply about experience, performance, and ease of use.

**Why now?**

A new generation of investors is emerging: ambitious, involved, done with taboos around money. We see a world where investing empowers everybody to live the life they've always dreamt of. To fuel that, we raised €40M from Hedosophia, Y Combinator, and Speedinvest, alongside founders and operators like Steve Anavi & Alexandre Prot (Qonto), Matthieu Rouif (Photoroom), Eric Demuth (Bitpanda), Axel Weber (former UBS Chairman), and Harsh Sinha (CTO at Wise).

In July 2026, the AMF granted us our MiCA license, on top of our Investment Firm license: one of the very few French platforms holding both, offering stocks, ETFs and crypto on a single regulated platform, right as Europe consolidates around licensed players. There's never been a more exciting time to join.

**What we offer**

We're 70 builders who genuinely love what they do: real ownership from day one, tier-1 salary and equity, offices in the heart of Paris with hybrid remote, and quarterly gatherings we actually look forward to.

We hire A-players who are as kind as they are demanding, people whose ideas transform not just our product but the way we work and think. Our culture is direct, transparent, and built on radical candor: we challenge each other openly, then commit. And we don't hedge on AI. It's the single most important skill of the next decade and a real bar here. Everyone at Finary has rebuilt how they work around it. If that's already second nature to you, you'll be surrounded by people pushing that frontier every day.

Read more about our values [here](https://finarywealth.notion.site/About-Finary-2f5919045b5d8060afd1d4e887ac550f?pvs=143).

## Context: where you'd have impact

Finary (YC W21, 25M€ Series B) is building the leading wealth management platform in Europe. Some numbers:

- **1M+ users** on the platform
- A YouTube channel with **850k+ subscribers and 5-10M monthly views**, our main acquisition engine
- **Finary One**, our private offering for 1M€+ portfolios, growing fast

Our #1 growth challenge: **converting our 1M+ users into paying subscribers** to drive revenue.

Our #2: feeding **qualified leads to Finary One** through content and growth work. The growth team today is 2 people plus AI agents doing the work of many more.

Everything you ship moves a metric someone looks at weekly.

Nothing you do will be "intern work" that sits in a drawer.

## About the role

You will join as a Growth Intern with a hybrid scope: hands-on growth execution across channels, plus data and automation work that makes the whole team faster. The team is AI-native: we automate everything that can be automated and spend our time on what moves the needle. This is not a "watch and learn" internship. You ship from week 1.

## Missions

**Growth execution**

- Create and manage content across platforms (YouTube, LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok)
- Support SEO and website work: blog articles, optimization, keyword research
- Build and optimize CRM campaigns to convert free users into subscribers
- Assist on paid marketing: campaign setup, monitoring, optimization
- Support Finary One lead generation, partnerships, PR, and brand initiatives

**Data & automation**

- Build dashboards and reports to monitor performance across channels, including the YouTube-to-signup funnel
- Design and implement automations to eliminate repetitive marketing and data workflows
- Leverage AI tools extensively: agents, workflows, analysis, reporting
- Bring data-driven recommendations to editorial and marketing meetings

## What we look for

✅ **Must-haves**

- **AI-first mindset**: uses AI daily to solve problems and accelerate work, beyond simple chat prompts
- **High agency**: acts without waiting for permission and drives tasks to completion
- **Analytical rigor**: structures problems, defines metrics, extracts clear insights from noisy data
- **Strong written communication** in French and English
- **Genuine interest** in personal finance and Finary's mission

✨ **Nice to have**

- Python or no-code automation experience (n8n, Make, Zapier)
- Familiarity with marketing analytics tools
- A personal project that shows initiative

🚫 **Dealbreakers**

- Low agency
- Tool-first thinking without judgment
- No interest in finance

## Why Finary now

- Series B momentum, building the #1 wealth management platform in Europe
- Full-stack growth exposure, not siloed: acquisition, conversion, retention, lead gen
- A-player team with high standards and a fast learning curve
- Real ownership and tangible outcomes shipped in weeks, not months

L’unité DTIPDT recherche, pour son service d’études et de développement thermohydraulique, un(e) stagiaire F/H préparant un diplôme d’ingénieur dans le domaine de la mécanique des fluides.

Dans le cadre de la modernisation des outils de calcul de sûreté utilisés pour la conception et le dimensionnement des réacteurs nucléaires, Framatome développe des méthodes basées sur le code CATHARE 3 afin de remplacer progressivement certaines approches historiques.

L’objectif est d’améliorer les méthodes utilisées pour étudier l’évolution de la puissance d’un réacteur après un arrêt automatique, tout en garantissant les marges de sûreté requises. * Réaliser des simulations au moyen du code de calcul à l’échelle système CATHARE 3 de transitoires de calcul de décroissance de puissance à la suite d’un arrêt d’urgence ;
* Confronter les résultats des calculs à des études de référence réalisées avec le code de calcul MANTA ;
Recenser, catégoriser et classifier les méthodes historiques ;
* Mettre en œuvre une nouvelle méthode d’étude sur la base des analyses précédentes ;
* Réaliser une campagne de tests de la nouvelle méthode par confrontation aux résultats historiques, analyser les différences et les gains potentiels ;
* Documenter l’ensemble des travaux.

**À propos de nous**

Chez Upvest, notre mission est de rendre l’investissement aussi simple que dépenser de l’argent. Upvest permet aux entreprises de proposer une large gamme de produits d’investissement et la meilleure expérience en matière d’investissement sur les marchés de capitaux et d’épargne retraite. Notre Investment API s’intègre facilement, pour que les fintechs et les institutions financières puissent se concentrer pleinement sur leur cœur de métier.

Nous travaillons avec les principales fintechs et institutions financières européennes, comme DKB, Revolut, N26 et Raisin. Fondée en 2017 par Martin Kassing, Upvest réunit aujourd’hui plus de 270 professionnels de plus de 70 nationalités. Upvest a levé 280 M€ auprès d’investisseurs de premier plan, dont BlackRock, Tencent, Sapphire Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, Earlybird, Notion Capital et Motive. Notre dernier tour de table de 105 M€, en mars 2026 et mené par Sapphire et Tencent, accélère notre croissance et nous permet d’offrir une expérience d’investissement haut de gamme.

**Le poste**

En 2027, Upvest lance le Plan d’Épargne en Actions (PEA) sur le marché français avec plusieurs fintechs de premier plan. Au sein de l’équipe Settlements & Transfers, vous intervenez sur l’ensemble de la chaîne post-marché des transferts de comptes-titres et de PEA : du traitement des instructions au dénouement chez Euroclear France, en passant par les relations avec les teneurs de compte, les dépositaires et les émetteurs.

Ce stage vous offre une exposition directe au post-marché français et européen dans une phase de lancement, avec de réelles responsabilités dès les premières semaines.

**Vos missions**

- **Transferts entrants et sortants :** Prendre en charge les transferts de comptes-titres (CTO) et de PEA avec les banques et courtiers en France et en Europe, de la réception de la demande jusqu’au dénouement des titres et des espèces.
- **Relations contreparties et clients :** Assurer une communication fluide avec les contreparties (banques, courtiers, dépositaires) et nos clients, et piloter le suivi des demandes et des relances.
- **Contrôles et réconciliations :** Vérifier les positions titres et espèces, rapprocher les mouvements avec notre dépositaire et analyser les écarts.
- **Gestion des suspens et des anomalies :** Analyser les instructions non dénouées ou rejetées, en identifier l’origine et coordonner leur résolution avec les contreparties et les équipes internes.
- **Fiscalité du PEA :** Contrôler et intégrer les bordereaux d’information (BI) afin de garantir la continuité de l’historique fiscal du plan.
- **Titres au nominatif :** Traiter les opérations sur titres nominatifs (conversions, inscriptions, radiations).
- **Reporting et amélioration continue :** Suivre activement les SLA et les KPI, rédiger les procédures et identifier des pistes d’automatisation.

**Votre profil**

- **Formation :** Master 1 ou 2 en finance, banque, économie ou droit (école de commerce, d’ingénieurs ou université), en année de césure ou jeune diplômé(e) d’un Master, avec possibilité de signer une convention de stage. Pour les M1 : votre établissement doit permettre un stage de 6 mois à temps plein (semestre intégré ou dispense de cours).
- **Langues :** Français langue maternelle (indispensable) et anglais courant.
- **Expérience :** Une première expérience en banque, back-office, middle-office ou opérations titres est un réel atout, tout comme une connaissance du PEA, du post-marché ou d’Euroclear France.
- **Motivation :** Un véritable intérêt pour les marchés de capitaux et les opérations post-marché.
- **Esprit d’analyse :** Rigueur, sens du détail et goût pour la résolution de problèmes complexes.
- **Outils :** Bonne maîtrise d’Excel / Google Sheets ; la connaissance de SQL/Python est un plus.

**Pourquoi nous rejoindre**

- **Un travail à fort impact :** Nous construisons l’infrastructure qui portera l’avenir de l’investissement en Europe. C’est complexe, ambitieux et porteur de sens. Vous travaillerez avec des technologies modernes et créerez quelque chose de totalement nouveau, sans système hérité et sans limites.
- **Moments d’équipe :** Participez aux événements d’entreprise comme UpFest, les dîners, les offsites et la fête de fin d’année, pour échanger avec vos collègues et célébrer nos réussites.
- **Inclusion :** Nous nous engageons pour une culture où chacun a sa place et s’épanouit. Nos groupes de ressources pour les employés favorisent l’inclusion et les liens, comme Upfem Black at Upvest, Up&Out et UpVergent.

**Nos valeurs**

- **Make it easy for others.** Nous simplifions le complexe et agissons avec les meilleures intentions.
- **Own the outcome.** Nous sommes proactifs, rapides et confiants pour faire avancer les choses : le progrès avant la perfection.
- **Rise to the challenge.** Nous visons haut et repoussons les limites. Nous restons curieux, apprenons et célébrons nos réussites ensemble.
- **Tell the story.** Nous commençons par le « pourquoi ». Nous sommes transparents et partageons nos connaissances pour inspirer les autres.

Upvest garantit l’égalité des chances. Nous célébrons la diversité et nous nous engageons à créer un environnement inclusif pour tous. À compétences égales, tous nos postes sont ouverts aux personnes en situation de handicap.

description:
**Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.**

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

## About the Role

This is an internship for an exceptional molecular biologist who wants to do the most serious work of their life so far. You won't shadow people or run busywork — you'll own real production workflows: cloning, protein expression, purification, and characterization, on the systems that serve our customers every day.

We run a high-throughput, heavily automated lab, and we hold interns to the same bar as the rest of the team. We'll give you hard problems and a senior person to learn from, and expect you to make a real dent. For us, an internship is also the best way to find people we want to keep — do great work, and we'll want to bring you on full-time afterwards.

## What You'll Do

- Run molecular cloning and protein production end to end: PCR, assembly, transformation, expression (bacterial and/or mammalian), and purification.
- Execute and improve QC on constructs and proteins (capillary electrophoresis, sequencing, SDS-PAGE) and characterization assays (binding, expression, stability).
- Take a workflow that's flaky or slow and make it reliable and faster — better protocols, better automation, fewer failures.
- Work hands-on with liquid handlers and lab automation, and help push manual protocols toward automated ones.
- Bring rigor to your data: document precisely, track samples, and make your results reproducible and traceable.
- Diagnose failures across biology, reagents, and instruments — and fix them, not just flag them.

## What We're Looking For

- **Strong hands already.** You've done real molecular biology — PCR, cloning, transformation, electrophoresis, ideally protein expression and purification — through research, a project, or a prior internship, and you're good at it. Protocols don't intimidate you.
- **BSc / MSc student or recent graduate** in molecular biology, biochemistry, or a relevant field.
- **Automation- and software-curious.** You'd rather automate a tedious step than repeat it 200 times. Comfort with scripting (Python) or liquid-handling automation is a strong plus.
- **Self-starter.** You see what needs doing and do it, without waiting for someone to hand you the next step.
- **AI-native.** It's 2026 — you use AI tools as a default to learn faster and work smarter.
- **High standards and high drive.** You care that the experiment is right, you move fast, and you're excited that the robots run real customer experiments.

## Details

- **Location:** Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)
- **Type:** Full time
- **Start date:** Flexible
- **Duration:** Minimum 6 months

**Application deadline**

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

### **Mission**

Rejoins l’équipe **R&D de notre unité E2C** en tant que **stagiaire conception Hardware pour chauffe-eau thermodynamique (F/H)**, à partir de septembre 2026 pour une durée de **6 mois**, au sein de notre site de La Roche-sur-Yon (85).

Dans le cadre du développement de nouveaux chauffe-eau thermodynamiques, tu contribueras à concevoir des architectures électroniques compétitives, en particulier pour les produits d’entrée de gamme.

**Accompagné mais autonome**
Ton tuteur, **Yves, Concepteur Hardware au sein de l’unité E2C**, sera là pour te former, te challenger et te laisser prendre ta place sur un véritable projet de conception.

Concrètement, tu vas :

* **Analyser les besoins et définir les solutions électroniques** : benchmark, identification des fonctions et définition des architectures adaptées aux contraintes produit.
* **Concevoir l’architecture hardware** : choix des composants, schémas, dimensionnement et définition des interfaces électriques et de communication.
* **Intégrer et prototyper les cartes électroniques** : intégration des fonctions (puissance, IHM…), placement/routage et participation à la réalisation des prototypes.
* **Valider la robustesse des solutions** : définition et réalisation des essais électriques, fonctionnels et environnementaux, puis analyse des résultats.
* **Améliorer et capitaliser** : analyse des anomalies, résolution des problèmes et documentation des choix de conception et solutions retenues.

## Hi, we’re Back Market.

We’re here to help **make tech reliable, affordable, and better than new**. We're a global marketplace for refurbished devices, helping lower our collective environmental impact by providing trustworthy, affordable tech with 92% less carbon emissions than new.

Yep, you read that right. Turns out refurbished tech is way better for the planet than new. In fact, With every device purchased on Back Market, our positive impact on the planet grows. From our Customer Care representatives to our software engineer, every individual at Back Market cuts the planet — and consumers — a break. **Our mission is simple: to do more with what we already have.**

Are you ready to join us?

## **JOB DESCRIPTION:**

Back Market is building AI-powered customer care experiences through Fin, its customer-facing AI Agent. Fin helps customers with pre-sales questions, delivery tracking, and technical troubleshooting.

As an AI Quality & Evaluation Intern, you will work with the QA Lead to monitor Fin’s performance, review conversations, identify recurring issues, and help improve the quality evaluation process. You will collaborate with content, product, data, and engineering teams to turn your findings into concrete improvements.

## **YOUR MISSION (IF YOU ACCEPT IT): 🥇**

- Operate and improve quality monitors and scorecards covering accuracy, policy compliance, connector use, escalation quality, tone, hallucinations, and unsupported claims.
- Review flagged and unflagged conversations to identify false positives, false negatives, and recurring defects.
- Prepare the weekly quality review by summarizing key findings, risks, and root causes.
- Analyse Fin’s performance across markets, languages, use cases, and rollout phases.
- Monitor handovers to human agents and customer satisfaction signals.
- Track corrective actions, owners, and validation status.
- Improve the documentation and versioning of Fin’s evaluation framework.
- Share clear, actionable feedback with product, engineering, content, and data teams.

## **YOU ARE IN THE RIGHT PLACE IF: ⭐**

- You are completing a Master 2 degree in Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, or another engineering discipline.
- You have strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- You are comfortable working with data and investigating anomalies.
- You are interested in generative AI, machine learning, or LLM evaluation.
- You can structure and communicate findings clearly in English.
- You are curious, detail-oriented, pragmatic, and comfortable investigating ambiguous problems.
- You can distinguish facts, hypotheses, and open questions.

BONUS POINT : Experience with LLM evaluation, prompt evaluation, conversational AI, or human-in-the-loop systems is a plus. French is helpful but not required.

## **ABOUT THE INTERNSHIP:**

- Start date: January 2027
- Duration : 6 months
- Full-time internship (35h/week)
- Location : Paris (France)

## **RECRUITMENT PROCESS: 📅**

- Skill fit interview and live case study with a team member (45min)
- Video-call Interview with the Talent Acquisition Specialist (30 min)
- Cultural fit interview with the manager (30min)

## **WHY SHOULD YOU JOIN US ? ✌🏼**

At Back Market, we’re committed to hiring and supporting diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives — it’s one of the reasons we’re such a high-scoring certified B Corp company (93.2).

No matter your role and seniority level, you’ll enjoy impact-driven work with hands-on career development in an innovative, driven, and fast-paced environment — with benefits to match, like:

- A mission driven work environment where your day to day makes an impact on the planet. Seriously.

- Hybrid work environment, with 2 remote days a week and 1 remote work week per quarter, plus 3 flex days.

- Employee Resource Groups, including mentorship programs, comprehensive accessibility policies, and cultural competency training.

At Back Market, we strive to create a workplace that embodies the world we’re trying to change. We’ve embedded our diversity, equity, and inclusion principles into our DNA — from dedicated staff to employee resource groups to our company values.

We know that the perfect background for a role doesn’t mean the perfect fit — we encourage you to apply for a role even if you think you may not have all the qualifications.

If reasonable accommodations are needed for the interview process, please do not hesitate to discuss this with the Talent Acquisition Team.

## **Build the Future of Climate Tech with Phlair**

**We're solving humanity's biggest challenge, and it takes everything we've got.**

The world needs more energy, not less. Fossil fuels powered our economy for decades, at the cost of our planet. At Phlair, we're inverting that equation with breakthrough electrochemical Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology that pulls CO₂ from the air for permanent storage or repurposing into carbon-negative chemicals.

**We're not here to play it safe. We're here to win.**

## **Why We’re Different?**

We solve hard problems and are product-first. Our *hydrolyzer-based Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology, enabling scalable and low-cost CO2 capture from ambient air. The electrochemical technology allows off-the-shelf components and is ideally suited to the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources.*

With proven offtake agreements from **customers such as** *Google, McKinsey, JPMorganChase, Shopify, Stripe, H&M, and Deep Sky;* we're one of only seven DAC companies with real market validation.

**Project Dawn** isn't just our flagship; it's our shot to scale CO₂ removal globally.

## **Is this a fit for me?**

**We're building for the 3-5% who are energized by winning and thrive under pressure.** Our pace demands people who see excellence as non-negotiable and execution as everything. We cherish work-life-harmony, not balance. If you need extensive structure or prefer playing it safe, we're probably not the right fit.

**Don't tick every box?** We value potential and spikes over perfect resumes. If you believe you can contribute to our mission at this intensity level, tell us why.

## Your mission at Phlair

As a **Growth & Operations Intern**, you support Phlair’s commercial and go-to-market efforts across customer research, pipeline development, and strategic analysis. You work closely with the commercial team, CEO, and technical teams to help turn technology progress into real market traction.

This role is ideal if you want to understand how deep-tech climate companies sell, position themselves, and navigate regulation-driven markets.

## What You’ll Work On

- Support go-to-market and business development efforts
- Help structure and maintain CRM data, sales funnels, and market intelligence
- Build AI-enabled workflows and automations using Claude skills/code; provide hands-on support on building a new automation backbone
- Prepare materials for outreach, meetings, conferences, and RFPs, including briefings, slides, and summaries, using tools like Figma
- All kinds of operational tasks beyond core comms work; you jump in wherever needed

This is not a “shadowing” internship. You’ll do real work that matters.

## What You Bring

- Availability from Q1/2027 onwards, at least six months.

- Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a Bachelor’s or Master’s program in business, engineering, natural sciences, economics, or a related field
- Prior internship experience in startups, consulting, sales, or venture is a plus, but not required
- Strong interest in climate tech, carbon removal, energy, or industrial decarbonization
- Hands-on experience with AI tools and automation workflows, or strong curiosity to apply AI in commercial and operational contexts
- Analytical mindset with the ability to structure information and communicate clearly in writing and presentations
- High ownership mentality, reliability, and comfort working in a fast-moving, unstructured environment

## **How we work at Phlair**

- **Onsite & Collaborative**: Our offices in Ismaning, Germany, house our pilot plant, where we work physically on our product every day. The team collaborates closely in the office, five days a week.

## **What We Offer?**

- **Competitive salary**
- **20 vacation days**
- **Public transport** pass for all of Germany
- **Relocation** support to help you settle into Munich
- **Fitness and wellness** benefits to keep you at your best
- **Fresh team lunches**, prepared by our amazing chef, Amelie

## **Learn more about Phlair**

- [Our Mission, Vision and Team](https://phlair.com/careers)
- [Phlair Secures Frontier’s First Electrochemical DAC Deal](https://frontierclimate.com/writing/phlair)
- [Technology Behind Phlair](https://techcrunch.com/2024/09/19/phlairs-carbon-sucking-technology-could-lower-direct-air-captures-costs/)
- [The Future of DAC](https://medium.com/extantia-capital/will-direct-air-capture-ever-be-affordable-the-rise-of-dac-3-0-d46cb355f35c)

**Not ticking every box? No problem.** We value potential and are open to considering a combination of education and experience instead of strictly following the listed requirements. ## Hi, we’re Back Market.

We’re here to help **make tech reliable, affordable, and better than new**. We're a global marketplace for refurbished devices, helping lower our collective environmental impact by providing trustworthy, affordable tech with 92% less carbon emissions than new.

Yep, you read that right. Turns out refurbished tech is way better for the planet than new. In fact, With every device purchased on Back Market, our positive impact on the planet grows. From our Customer Care representatives to our software engineer, every individual at Back Market cuts the planet — and consumers — a break. **Our mission is simple: to do more with what we already have.**

Are you ready to join us?

The Trade-In service enables customers to sell their old devices (smartphones, tablets, gaming consoles, Back Market’s network professional refurbishers. This is great for the consumer who can reclaim cash for their old device and prevent the accumulation of e-waste in our landfills. Trade-In is also a key pillar for Back Market as it facilitates the sourcing of tech devices to be refurbished and sold on our website.

BuyBulk is Back Market's centralized Trade-in service where a single professional processing partner receives, tests and grades all incoming devices on behalf of the refurbishers. Instead of each refurbisher individually sourcing and processing trade-in devices, BuyBulk handles the entire operational process and ships the tested devices in bulk. This service removes the sourcing burden and lets professionals focus on what they do best: refurbishing and selling.

## **YOUR MISSION (IF YOU ACCEPT IT): 🥇**

**Play a key role in ensuring Buybulk performance reaches targets on a daily / weekly / monthly basis by:**

- Tracking and monitoring KPIs to help the team understand performance drivers and take relevant actions: you will support the team in regular reporting, one-off analyses on specific topics and continuous improvement of reporting and tools
- Being in charge of key operational processes and checks to ensure a steady performance and customer satisfaction

**Support the team on major projects - examples of projects and topics you could work on:**

- Improving efficiency through automation (simplify / automate processes, reportings, analyses, alerting …)
- Build new or improve existing processes, tools and reports on ad-hoc projects (quality control, customer care, pricing, …)
- Participate in structuring large projects by identifying opportunities (benchmark, research, …), setting up action plans, identifying stakeholders (within teams such business development, marketing or product), defining timelines and success factors and regularly following up on progress

## **YOU ARE IN THE RIGHT PLACE IF: ⭐**

- You are looking for a **6-month internship**
- **English and French fluency** (fully professional capability).
- You have **advanced analytical and data** manipulation skills and exceptional attention to written, visual, and quantitative detail
- You have advanced **Gsheet** skills (incl. pivot tables, complex formulas, …) ; you have **basics of SQL** - or willingness to learn during the internship ; VBA, Zapier and any automation or visualization tool/software is a big plus
- You are eager to test and learn by yourself and to proactively identify areas of improvement and implement solutions
- Ideally you have previous experience (internship, freelance, apprenticeship) as a business analyst, country or category manager, operations manager (logistics, customer care, …), seller success manager, investment banking or consulting intern/junior and you are looking for a hands-on experience allowing you to have a concrete impact on the business.

## **ABOUT THE INTERNSHIP:**

- Start date: January 2027
- Duration : 6 months
- Full-time internship (35h/week)
- Location : Paris (France)

## **RECRUITMENT PROCESS: 📅**

- Business case (live) with a member of the team
- Skills & cultural fit interview with the direct manager
- Video-call Interview with the Talent Acquisition Specialist

## **WHY SHOULD YOU JOIN US ? ✌🏼**

At Back Market, we’re committed to hiring and supporting diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives — it’s one of the reasons we’re such a high-scoring certified B Corp company (93.2).

No matter your role and seniority level, you’ll enjoy impact-driven work with hands-on career development in an innovative, driven, and fast-paced environment — with benefits to match, like:

- A mission driven work environment where your day to day makes an impact on the planet. Seriously.

- Hybrid work environment, with 2 remote days a week and 1 remote work week per quarter, plus 3 flex days.

- Employee Resource Groups, including mentorship programs, comprehensive accessibility policies, and cultural competency training.

At Back Market, we strive to create a workplace that embodies the world we’re trying to change. We’ve embedded our diversity, equity, and inclusion principles into our DNA — from dedicated staff to employee resource groups to our company values.

We know that the perfect background for a role doesn’t mean the perfect fit — we encourage you to apply for a role even if you think you may not have all the qualifications.

- Collect and format sets of terms describing pathologies, allergies, treatments, and other medical concepts, based on standard medical terminologies such as ICD-10 and SNOMED CT.
- Adapt medical labels to create versions that are understandable to patients and healthcare professionals.
- Translate labels from English into German.

## **Company Overview**

In July 2026, Cheiron announced an **$8 million seed round led by Menlo Ventures**, bringing total funding to **$13 million** to date, with the backing and strategic support of industry veterans including Moderna co-founder and MIT Institute Professor Robert Langer, former Pfizer Chief Medical Officer Freda Lewis-Hall, Chai Discovery co-founder and CEO Josh Meier, former Starbucks CEO Laxman Narasimhan, and former Apple AI chief John Giannandrea.

Cheiron is building the first AI-native operating system designed to represent an entire drug program as a single connected system. The company's platform helps biopharma teams represent, reason over, and stress-test the full state of a drug development program, including the claims, evidence, assumptions, risks, decisions, and commitments that determine whether a therapy advances. In less than six months since launch, Cheiron has been adopted by tens of thousands of biopharma professionals and deployed by major drug developers, and is already used by 7 of Korea's top 10 biopharma companies.

Cheiron is expanding into pharmaceutical CMC (Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls) teams. CMC governs how a drug is made, tested, and kept consistent across its entire commercial life. The work involves hundreds of regulatory commitments, post-approval changes, and cross-market submissions. Today it runs on documents, spreadsheets, and institutional memory. Cheiron augments manual workflows with a CMC regulatory-specific intelligence and reasoning layer.

Founded in 2024 by Stanford-trained AI researchers. The team includes leaders with combined decades of experience across pharma and biotech. Headquartered in **Los Altos, California**. We are building and deploying the product now with rapid expansion into global markets.

Nous participons ainsi à leur montée en compétences au travers de notre école de formation interne, encourageons la promotion interne et accordons l’égalité des chances lors de nos recrutements. #ActivateurDeProgrès

**Description du poste**
------------------------

La simulation numérique des écoulements est un outil central de la conception industrielle. Pour représenter finement les chocs ou les sillages, un calcul demande des maillages de plusieurs millions de mailles et peut durer plusieurs heures. Or une étude de conception ou d’optimisation demande des centaines, voire des milliers de calculs. Les méthodes classiques de réduction de modèle, fondées sur des bases linéaires, représentent mal les structures qui se déplacent avec les paramètres, comme un choc.

Les modèles génératifs (diffusion, *flow matching*... ) offrent une autre approche. Ils apprennent la loi des solutions et produisent des champs nets, là où une régression classique a tendance à les lisser. Dans un contexte industriel, ils permettent de réutiliser les bases de calculs existantes, d’obtenir une prédiction bien plus vite qu’avec un solveur, d’estimer l’incertitude ou de fournir au solveur un champ initial qui accélère sa convergence.

Un premier stage, réalisé en 2026 dans l’équipe-projet Inria/ONERA MONHADE, a produit une base d’environ 30 000 solutions des équations d’Euler 2D et entraîné des modèles déterministes et génératifs sur des maillages d’environ 20 000 mailles. Ces modèles donnent des prédictions précises et accélèrent nettement la convergence du solveur, mais généralisent encore mal à des géométries non vues pendant l’entraînement. Il reste aussi à traiter des maillages de taille industrielle, à réduire le coût des modèles génératifs et à évaluer ces méthodes dans des conditions proches d’un usage industriel.

Le stage s’appuiera sur l’expertise des ingénieurs docteurs d’Ingeliance et sur des réunions régulières avec l’équipe MONHADE. Le ou la stagiaire aura accès aux moyens de calcul du CCRT, ainsi qu’aux données et aux codes du stage précédent. De nouvelles simulations pourront être réalisées si besoin.

L’objectif de ce stage est de poursuivre le développement de ces approches génératives. Le projet se décompose selon les tâches suivantes :

* Étude bibliographique, prise en main des résultats du stage précédent et des outils de production des données d’entraînement ;
* Développement et comparaison de plusieurs approches :

– **Espaces latents** : compresser les champs pour entraîner le modèle génératif dans un espace de petite dimension, et augmenter la taille du maillage ;

– **Prédictions locales** : entraîner un modèle sur des sous-domaines, puis le faire glisser sur le domaine pour couvrir des champs plus grands. Une approche locale pourrait aussi mieux généraliser à de nouvelles géométries ;

– **Ponts de Schrödinger** : passer directement d’un champ à un autre plutôt que de partir d’un bruit gaussien, afin de réduire le nombre d’étapes de prédiction ;

* Évaluation de ces méthodes dans un contexte industriel et comparaison avec un solveur : précision, capacité de généralisation à des géométries et des régimes non vus pendant l’entraînement, coût total, accélération du solveur.

**Profil recherché**
--------------------

* **Étudiant·e en 2ème ou 3ème année d’école d’ingénieur**, avec une appétence pour la recherche et une grande curiosité ;
* Notions d’apprentissage profond et de programmation en Python ;
* Envie d’entrer dans le détail mathématique de la construction de ces modèles ;
* Connaissances en simulation numérique, en particulier en mécanique des fluides.

**Description du poste**
------------------------

La simulation numérique des écoulements est un outil central de la conception industrielle. Chaque calcul est coûteux, et les bases de calculs ne couvrent souvent que quelques valeurs des paramètres. Entre ces valeurs, les méthodes de réduction de modèle fondées sur des bases linéaires représentent mal les structures qui se déplacent, comme un choc ou un sillage : interpoler linéairement deux solutions donne deux chocs atténués au lieu d’un seul.

L’interpolation par déformation traite ce problème en deux temps. Une application déforme d’abord le domaine pour aligner les structures des deux solutions, puis les champs alignés sont interpolés. L’approche est non intrusive : elle n’utilise que des solutions déjà calculées et demande peu de données.

Une thèse menée chez Ingeliance avec l’équipe-projet Inria/ONERA MONHADE a développé une méthode qui calcule cette déformation directement à partir des champs, par minimisation d’une fonctionnelle différentiée avec JAX. Sur des écoulements avec chocs et sillages, elle est plus précise que l’interpolation linéaire. Deux limites demeurent : la déformation est définie sur des boîtes rectangulaires, ce qui complique les conditions aux limites autour des obstacles, et les solutions doivent être projetées sur une grille cartésienne, alors que les calculs industriels utilisent des maillages non structurés.

Le stage s’appuiera sur l’expertise des ingénieurs docteurs d’Ingeliance et sur des réunions avec l’équipe MONHADE. Le ou la stagiaire aura accès aux moyens de calcul du CCRT, ainsi qu’aux codes et aux données de la thèse.

L’objectif de ce stage est de lever ces deux limites et d’évaluer la méthode sur des cas industriels. Le projet se décompose selon les tâches suivantes :

* Étude bibliographique, prise en main des codes et des cas tests de la thèse ;
* Formulation en vitesse : obtenir la déformation et son inverse en intégrant un même champ de vitesse, sur lequel s’imposent les conditions aux limites (vitesse nulle ou tangente aux parois) ;
* Maillages non structurés : évaluer la fonctionnelle directement sur le maillage de calcul, sans projection sur une grille ;

description:
Ekimetrics is the European leader in data science, with over 500 data scientists and 1,000+ projects since 2006. With offices in Paris, London, New York, and Hong Kong, we conduct projects in over 50 countries across various sectors, including financial services, retail, telecom, healthcare, and more.

Our mission is to help companies audit their data opportunities, enhance their analytical capital, and deploy actionable solutions that maximize their marketing and operational performance while reinvigorating business models.

Our absolute focus is on delivering short-term gains while ensuring the long-term development of our clients' data capital. We are committed to offering the most advanced data science approaches and building ethical, sustainable AI practices.

Key Figures

- 20 years of experience in data science

- 500+ data scientists, all consultants

- 5 offices in Paris, London, New York, Hong Kong, and Shanghai

- 350+ clients (CAC40, Fortune500)

- $1M+ in profit generated for our clients since 2006

- 1,000+ data science projects

Within Ekimetrics, the Innovation Department works on AI research topics in collaboration with our industrial and academic partners. The department comprises several PhD experts in generative AI, deep learning, computer vision, time series, explainability, and causality. Each expert leads teams tasked with studying and building state-of-the-art methods and adapting them to specific business problems, developing new methodologies or algorithms to address identified challenges, and ensuring a seamless handover for integration within Ekimetrics' industrial ecosystem.

A central focus of the Innovation Department is closing the gap between cutting-edge AI agents and the day-to-day reality of delivering data science at scale. The department is investing in agentic systems that accelerate the data science lifecycle while keeping data scientists firmly in control of quality, governance, and business relevance. This internship sits at the heart of that effort, combining applied AI research with production-grade engineering on Ekimetrics' modern data stack.

Internship Objective: From a Business Question to a Trusted Recommendation

LLM-based agents have made rapid progress in the past two years: they can now write, run and tune machine learning code with little human help. Yet real data science projects rarely start from a clean, well-defined task. They start from a business question and imperfect data, and the early choices (what to predict, how to measure success, how to validate) decide whether the result can be trusted. Automating these steps calls for assistants that know when to ask, when to stop, and how to back every claim with evidence.

The Innovation Department is building remit, a harness that semi-automates the data science workflow. At each step of a project (framing, data design, exploratory analysis, modeling, evaluation), AI agents draft the output, automatic checks catch common mistakes such as data leakage, and a data scientist reviews and accepts the result before moving on. Ultimately, a business user brings a question and a dataset, and the system frames the problem, prepares and explores the data, compares models against a simple baseline, and returns a clear recommendation in which every figure can be traced back to the data.

The work builds on recent research in agentic data science [1]. Agents now earn medals on many of the Kaggle competitions in MLE-bench [2], yet they tend to guess silently rather than ask when a task is ambiguous [3]. Meanwhile, tabular foundation models such as TabICLv2 [4] give strong predictive models without any tuning.

The intern will work with senior data scientists and AI builders to build and refine remit. This internship offers an opportunity to engage with cutting-edge AI research and production engineering.

Key Responsibilities

The intern will:

- Review the latest research on agentic data science and on the evaluation of AI agents, building on the team's recent review.

- Design and implement remit's agents, starting with problem framing and data design, together with the automatic checks that catch mistakes such as data leakage.

- Help define how the system works with business users: when to ask a clarifying question, when to stop rather than guess, and how to explain results in plain language.

- Extend the system toward modeling and evaluation, building on trusted tools (scikit-learn, AutoML, tabular foundation models) rather than free-form generated code.

- Build a benchmark of realistic business cases, run experiments to measure quality, reliability and cost, and take part in a pilot with business users.

- Help integrate the system with the Databricks stack (Unity Catalog, MLflow) and support the safe and governed operation of the agents.

Profile

- Currently in the final year of a Master's or Engineering degree, with strong foundations in machine learning, statistics, and programming.

- Good grasp of model validation: train/test splits, data leakage, baselines.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work autonomously on an open-ended research-and-build problem and to explain results to non-specialists.

- Familiarity with large language models and agentic techniques (prompting, tool calling, structured outputs, evaluation).

- Strong Python skills and a solid command of the standard data science toolkit (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, gradient-boosting libraries).

- Fluency in English.

- Nice to have: experience with an agent framework, solid software engineering practices (git, code review, testing), and exposure to Databricks, MLflow or cloud data platforms.

Benefits

- Hands-on Research & Engineering Experience: Build a pioneering agentic system on real data science workflows, contributing to a tool with direct real-world impact.

- Collaborative Learning: Engage with a team of data scientists, AI experts, and PhDs in a dynamic, research-driven environment within Ekimetrics' Innovation Department.

- Skill Development: Gain expertise in LLM agents, the evaluation of AI systems, and production tooling on Databricks (Unity Catalog, MLflow).

- Career Growth: Opportunity to transition into a full-time Data Scientist role in AI at Ekimetrics, or into a PhD program, upon successful completion of the internship.

description:
Founded in 2020 and based in the heart of Paris, C12’s mission is to be at the center of one of the biggest technological breakthroughs of the century and change the course of history by building a universal quantum computer.

At C12, we believe that achieving a true breakthrough in quantum computing requires rethinking the fundamentals. That’s why our founders—deeply rooted in academic and engineering excellence—have chosen carbon nanotubes as the building blocks of our quantum processors. This ultra-pure material dramatically reduces error rates, boosts performance, and minimizes hardware overhead—key ingredients for scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computing. By crafting a unique approach that scales, we aim to revolutionize quantum computing just as silicon transformed classical computing.

Since our founding, we’ve raised over €25 million in funding, published 11 scientific papers, and secured 8 patents. Today, our fast-growing team of 80+, including 25 PhDs, has over 26 nationalities represented. We have our own cutting-edge lab spaces in Paris' historic Panthéon district, where scientists, engineers, and innovators work side-by-side to tackle some of the most exciting technical challenges of our time.

If you're passionate about shaping the future of quantum technology and want to make a real impact, C12 offers a unique environment to grow, learn, and innovate.

### Your role at C12:

An optimal qubit calibration is a necessary condition for a good and operational quantum computer. Calibrating qubits is a highly non-trivial task which requires playing with lots of parameters at the same time and due to design variability, must be performed from scratch for every new chip. Thankfully, recent advancements in AI and Machine Learning overcome these difficulties and help accelerate qubit calibration and quantum hardware research.

As part of the AI for Quantum team at C12, you will design, develop and deploy qubit calibration algorithms. Your goal will be to use AI and ML tools to automate certain phases of qubit calibration and, by doing so, support our Qubit Control team.

Your job will involve:

- Scientific reading (articles, open-source solutions, …)
- Implementation of cutting-edge algorithms for qubit calibration
- Writing and maintaining the code base for industrialisation purposes
- Testing and measuring on C12’s quantum chips

### About You:

- You are enrolled in a Master’s program in Physics, Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, or a related field
- You have an appetite for coding
- You are eager to learn physics and to interact with both scientists and developers on a daily basis

- You are proficient in Python
- You have good experience with AI and Machine Learning tools
- You have some knowledge of Quantum Computing or Quantum Physics
- You have a good level of English, both oral and written

**ABOUT MUSIXMATCH:**

Musixmatch is the leading music metadata company, featuring the world’s largest lyrics catalog and a community of over 80M contributors. Musixmatch is the trusted global partner of companies like Spotify, Apple, Amazon Music, Meta, Google, MTV, Shazam, Vevo, Tidal, Snapchat and has a partnership with more than 100,000 music publishers including Sony/ Music Publishing, Universal Music Publishing, Warner/Chappell, Kobalt, BMG Rights, and the Harry Fox Agency.

We are a bunch of creatives who care about our work and what we do. We believe that participation and collaboration are key to getting things done well. We are looking for tech-savvy people who are eager to learn in a fast-paced environment, who have an international outlook on life, and who love taking on new challenges.

**Position:**
We are looking for a Software Engineer Intern to join our Services Engineering team. This role is ideal for someone who wants hands-on experience building AI-powered tooling on top of a large-scale music catalog, working with real production data and modern cloud infrastructure. You'll help design and build an MCP-based (Model Context Protocol) ecosystem that gives our Operations team an AI-assisted toolchain for data investigation, metadata auditing, anomaly detection, and automated reporting, learning how production environments and agentic systems actually work. This is an extracurricular internship (tirocinio extracurriculare) lasting 6 months, with a monthly reimbursement of €800.

**Responsibilities:**
Explore and map the Recording music catalog architecture, spanning relational data (MySQL/Aurora) and non-relational document stores (DynamoDB)
Build specialized MCP servers, skills, and tools exposing catalog data, resources, and prompt templates to AI agents
Implement operations guardrails such as access controls, read-only permissions, rate limiting, and query execution safeguards, so agents can query live stores without compromising production stability
Instrument and monitor inference, context window, embedding, and query costs, treating cost as an engineering metric alongside accuracy and latency
Containerize services with Docker and deploy to Kubernetes via Helm using our standard Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform) workflow
Run staged testing with the Operations team, promote to production, and support a company-wide beta release
Debug, test, and improve backend services across the stack

**Requirements:**
Good knowledge of at least one of Node.js/TypeScript, Python, or PHP (backend development, async processing)
Basic understanding of database querying and modeling (SQL and/or NoSQL)
Interest in AI tooling, LLMs, and the Model Context Protocol (Tools, Resources, Prompts)
Interest in cloud technologies and DevOps (AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform are a plus)
Understanding of Git and collaborative development workflows
Problem-solving mindset and willingness to learn
Ability to work in English

# **WE CANNOT PROVIDE VISA SPONSORSHIP**

# Details

**Preferred starting date:** ASAP

**Weekly availability:** Full-time (5 days/week)

**Period:** 6 months

**Location:** Aerospace Innovation Hub, Delft, the Netherlands

# About the company

Fiducial is a young but fast-growing deep-tech start-up with big ambitions at the frontier of autonomy, perception, and defence. Currently, we are developing software for advanced onboard UAV situational awareness in military applications. Using low-cost and widely available sensors and compute, our solutions are built for scalability. From there, we plan to develop a line-up of interconnected solutions to safeguard European safety.

Our team consists of engineers who are passionate about the technology and solutions they develop. The only time most of us are not thinking about the technology is when we are asleep, and sometimes even then. Our team members come from different backgrounds such as Aerospace Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, Robotics, and Computer Graphics. Our office is located in the Aerospace Innovation Hub, a start-up hub on the TU Delft campus in the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering.

We work closely with top-tier partners, ranging from government agencies and prime contractors to academic research institutes and other start-ups. Our projects span from large tender orders in collaboration with partners to low-TRL research with government agencies. Whether through formal R&D programs or rapid prototyping tracks, we operate at the intersection of innovation and deployment.

# **The project**

Sensor calibration is a manual job today, and it does not scale to the number of sensor units we intend to ship. We are building automated test and calibration infrastructure to fix that, starting with a cell built around a UFactory UF850 robotic arm on a linear rail.

We already have the arm and the calibration software. What we do not have is the physical cell around it, or the software that drives it. This first project is split into two internships that run side by side:

• Mechanical design and integration — this position

• Robot programming and automation — separate posting

The two interns will work closely together. Neither half of this project is any good on its own. This calibration cell is the first thing we are building on this front, not the last, so there is a good chance the right person carries on to other hardware and automation projects once it is running.

**Your role**

If you are the kind of person who likes designing hardware that has to actually work, who thinks in tolerances and stiffness rather than only in shapes, and who wants to see something you drew get built, measured, and used every week, this internship is designed for you.

We are looking for a Mechanical Design & Integration Intern to help design and build the physical hardware behind our robotic test and automation infrastructure. Your first project is a cell built around a robotic arm and linear rail — but the skills involved are the same ones we’ll lean on for whatever we automate next.

Good automated hardware has to satisfy a few things that pull against each other, and balancing them is the interesting part of this kind of work:

1. **Modular.** It has to accept different payloads and fixtures without a redesign each time. Swapping the item under test should take minutes, not a morning.

2. **Movable.** It has to relocate: between rooms, into a van, onto a test site and back again. It cannot be a bolted-to-the-floor installation.

3. **Repeatable.** Moving it must not destroy the geometry. If re-establishing it after transport requires a full re-survey every time, we have not solved the problem.

Resolving that tension is yours to do, on this project and on whatever comes after it.

This is not a desk-only internship. You will spend time at the CAD workstation, but also at the printers, at the bench with a caliper in your hand, and underneath the frame wondering why it flexes.

**What you’ll do**

• Design the structural base and frame that carry the arm and the linear rail, with the stiffness and stability to move reliably and repeatably.

• Design a modular payload interface: quick-change mounts for cameras, rigs, and targets, so swapping the item under test is fast and doesn’t require re-measuring.

• Work out how the target and the item under test need to be presented to each other, and design the fixturing that makes that possible.

• Make the cell genuinely mobile: it needs to relocate without losing its geometry, and get back up and running quickly wherever it lands.

• Manage vibration, cabling, and safety (E-stops, guarding, keep-out zones) so the cell is reliable and safe to run unattended.

• Build, source, and assemble what you design in our workshop, then measure and characterise how well it actually performs.

• Document your work: CAD, drawings, BOM, and SOPs, so the cell is easy to operate, maintain, and hand over.

**Who you are**

• You are enrolled in a relevant study program (Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Precision Engineering, Aerospace, Robotics, or similar).

• You are fluent in CAD. We care that you can design, not which package you learned it in.

• You think in tolerances, stiffness, and error budgets, not only in geometry.

• You have built physical things, and you have had them not work the first time.

• You are comfortable in a workshop: hand tools, drill press, 3D printers, soldering iron, and a caliper you trust.

• You have design-for-manufacture instincts. You know roughly what is cheap to make and what is not, and you ask before you find out the expensive way.

• You are comfortable taking responsibility for a piece of hardware that other people depend on.

• You are independent, curious, organized, and resourceful.

• Linux does not scare you. You will need to jog the arm and pull data yourself rather than waiting for someone to do it for you.

We care much more about what you have designed, built, broken, and fixed than about grades.

**Nice to have**

These are strong pluses, but not strict requirements:

• Precision mechanism or metrology experience: kinematic and quasi-kinematic mounts, flexures, alignment techniques, GD&T

• Linear motion experience: profile rails, ball screws, belt drives, gantries, and their real-world error behaviour

• FEA (static and modal) plus the judgement to know when running it is worth the time

• Machining or sheet-metal design experience, and experience talking to suppliers

• Vibration measurement and damping

• Machine safety and CE marking awareness (ISO 12100, ISO 10218, ISO/TS 15066)

• Cameras, optics, lighting, or photogrammetry background

• Basic Python, enough to command the arm and read a sensor without help

• Experience with robotic cells, test rigs, or automated test equipment

**Please include**

When applying, please include photos, drawings, renders, or links to things that show us you actually design and build. For example:

• CAD models and technical drawings

• photos of hardware you built, ideally next to the thing you designed it to do

• fixtures, jigs, or test rigs

• 3D-printed or machined parts, and what you learned making them

• competition or society projects (Formula Student, DUT Racing, rocketry, robotics teams)

• repairs, teardowns, and modifications

• anything that demonstrates hands-on technical ownership

If you have ever built a fixture, measured it, found it flexed far more than you expected, and redesigned it until it didn’t, you’ll probably fit right in.

**Requirements**

• Enrolled in a relevant study program (Mechanical, Mechatronics, Precision Engineering, Aerospace, Robotics, or similar)

• Solid CAD skills

• Basic Linux skills

• Strong interest in robotics, precision hardware, test automation, or perception systems

• English proficiency

• Organized and proactive working style

**What we offer**

• 1000 euro monthly compensation

• 10 vacation days during the internship period

• Flexible working hours and the option to work from home where practical, though this project mostly lives in the workshop

• A direct and significant influence on highly innovative products

• The opportunity to work close to the hardware and the product, with fast iteration and tight feedback loops

• Full ownership of a self-contained system that the rest of the company will depend on

• A team environment where practical experimentation, learning, and ownership are expected

**The application procedure**

• If after reading the above you are convinced you are the right person for the job, send us some information about yourself. This can be a resume, website, portfolio, or any other source that gives us a clear impression of your background, technical skills, and hands-on experience.

• We will get back to you ASAP. If we think you could be a fit for the position, we will invite you for an informal introduction so we can get to know you, and equally important, you can get to know us. After this, a more technically focused interview may follow.

• If at that point we believe you are the person we are looking for, we will discuss the specifics such as starting date and internship period.

**Welcome to the team!**

Chez **FAIRMAT,** notre mission est de construire un écosystème circulaire qui préserve les matériaux avancés loin des décharges pour les remettre au cœur de la conception des produits.

Nous sommes une deeptech pionnière dans le recyclage de la fibre de carbone, offrant une solution complète reposant sur des technologies disruptives et des innovations en robotique. En 4 ans seulement, nous avons déjà réalisé des exploits impressionnants :

- Développé et scalé une usine dans la région nantaise

- Sécurisé plus de $73.7M de fonds auprès d’investisseurs

- Ouvert notre première filiale aux USA

- Conclut nos premiers contrats avec des acteurs industriels référence

Nous sommes à la recherche de talents engagés pour un avenir durable, enthousiastes à l’idée de rejoindre cette aventure industrielle.

**Votre rôle**

Au sein de notre laboratoire de Recherche & Développement de Paris, vous participez aux essais contribuant au développement de la technologie de recyclage Fairmat.

Vous travaillerez sur des projets de fond visant à améliorer la performance de nos matériaux afin de développer de nouveaux grades, pour de nouvelles applications produits.

**Vos missions**

### 1/Organiser et préparer les essais de développement

- Rédiger des plans d'essais
- Mener des campagnes de test au laboratoire dans l’optique d’améliorer le procédé de recyclage
- Préparer les paillasses en fonction des tests prévus
- S’assurer du bon fonctionnement des équipements et les maintenir en état, remonter toute anomalie ou dysfonctionnement

### 2/ Réaliser des manipulations

- Préparer les échantillons de matières premières et produits finis (moulage)
- Préparer les éprouvettes pour la réalisation des essais de caractérisation (découpe, usinage)
- Réaliser les tests de caractérisation : morphologiques (microscopie, rugosité …), mécaniques (traction, flexion, cisaillement…), chimiques et thermiques (DSC…)
- Proposer des améliorations et des suggestions de manipulations pour optimisation

### 3/ Restituer les résultats

- Synthétiser les résultats, rédiger des rapports d’essai et des comptes-rendus et les retranscrire dans notre base de donnée
- Interpréter et présenter les résultats lors des points périodiques
- Participer au développement des outils informatiques du bureau d'étude (base de données, gestion des informations).

**A World-Changing Company**

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

**The Role**

Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organisations around the world use data. As a Software Engineer Intern, you’ll have an opportunity to grow more quickly than you ever envisioned, as you contribute high-quality code directly to Palantir Gotham, Palantir Foundry, or Palantir Apollo: products that are deployed at some of the most important institutions across the public and private sectors. You'll create features used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters, in countries around the world. Palantir's Product Development organisation is made up of small teams of Software Engineers, each focusing on a specific aspect of a product. For example, you might join a team that builds a Foundry front-end application, or a component of the Gotham release infrastructure. We encourage communication and collaboration among teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different aspects of each product.

**Core Responsibilities**

As a Software Engineer, you are involved throughout the product lifecycle - from idea generation, design, and prototyping to execution and shipping while also being paired with a mentor dedicated to your growth and success. You'll collaborate closely with technical and non-technical counterparts to understand our customers' problems and build products that tackle them. One of the most effective ways to understand what our users need is to meet them. You may receive an opportunity to tour the assembly line at an auto-manufacturer or join a counter-terror analyst at their desk to really understand their mission and difficulties.

**SWE principles include:**

• Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end in spite of obstacles we may encounter.

• Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other Software Engineers, Product Managers, Designers and Product Reliability Engineers. We also partner with our business development teams (Forward Deployed Engineers, Deployment Strategists) in order to understand and solve our customers' problems.

• Trust: We trust each other to effectively handle time and priorities, and don't micromanage. We want people to have the space to think for themselves, while feeling supported by their team.

**Technologies We Use**

It doesn’t matter what languages you know when you join us, but it does matter that you can write clean, effective code and learn new languages quickly. Our software is constantly evolving, so we need engineers who can do the same. Alongside peers that bring diverse experience - whether you’re a former university TA, switched to CS recently, or are a hackathon enthusiast — you'll build your skills to apply the best technology to solve a given problem. Right now, we use:

• Varying languages, including Java and Go for backend and Typescript for frontend

• Open-source technologies like Cassandra, Spark, Elasticsearch, React, and Redux

• Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle, Webpack, and GitHub

### What We Value

- Ability to communicate and collaborate with a variety of individuals, including engineers, users and non-technical team members.
- Willingness to learn and make decisions independently, and the ability to ask questions when needed.

### What We Require

- Engineering background in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, and Physics.
- Familiarity with data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks, and other technical tools.
- Experience coding in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, JavaScript, or similar languages.
- Must be planning on graduating in 2028. This should be your final internship before graduating.

### To apply, please submit the following:

- An updated resume / CV - please do so in PDF format.
- Thoughtful responses to our application questions.

Faites décoller votre carrière : **Bienvenue au sein du Groupe INGELIANCE !**

Depuis plus de 25 ans, nous accompagnons nos clients dans l’étude et la réalisation de projets à forte technicité au travers de bureaux d’études (interne et sur site client), d’une offre de conseil et d’une cellule R&D.

Avec une équipe de plus de **700 professionnels passionnés** – Techniciens, Ingénieurs, Docteurs – répartis sur **20 sites** en France, nous cultivons l’innovation au quotidien pour une mission essentielle : **garantir la satisfaction de nos clients**.

Notre organisation se structure autour de deux divisions complémentaires (Développement Produits & Systèmes et Solutions Industrielles) et d'une Direction Technique.

Nous intervenons dans des secteurs d’avenir tels que le **naval, l**’**aéronautique, le spatial & défense, l**’**énergie et le nucléaire**, offrant ainsi des opportunités variées et stimulantes.

Nous avons à coeur d’accompagner l’ensemble de nos collaborateurs tout au long de leur carrière au sein du Groupe. Nous participons ainsi à leur montée en compétences au travers de notre école de formation interne, encourageons la promotion interne et accordons l’égalité des chances lors de nos recrutements. #ActivateurDeProgrès

**Description du poste**
------------------------

Dans le cadre des démarches R&T de notre équipe de simulation numérique, vous contribuerez au sein du pôle « Analyse multiphysiques » à développer nos connaissances en CFD sur les régimes d’écoulement laminaires / turbulents.

La transition d’une couche limite laminaire vers un régime turbulent constitue un phénomène important afin de déterminer les performances aérodynamiques d’un système. La position de la zone de transition influence directement les caractéristiques de l’écoulement en proche paroi. Il est donc nécessaire d’obtenir cette position de manière précise. En simulation numérique, la zone de transition est fortement dépendante du modèle de turbulence choisi.

L’objectif principal du stage est donc d’évaluer la pertinence, la précision et la robustesse des différents niveaux de modélisation de cette transition. Ces niveaux comprennent une approche RANS, URANS et éventuellement LES.

Les axes d’exploration seront les suivants :

* **Analyse bibliographique et recherche de cas expérimentaux** / Etudes numériques existantes.
* **Prise en main des outils OPENFOAM et ANSYS Fluent** afin de s’approprier les logiciels ainsi que l’environnement HPC relatifs au cluster de calcul interne.
* **Mises en données d’un cas test 2D puis 3D** pour comparer les résultats obtenus à l’aide de différents modèles présents dans chacun des logiciels.
* **Approche RANS**

Analyse de différents modèles de turbulence classiques et des modèles de transition (k-omega, k-epsilon, transition k-kl-omega, …).

* **Approche URANS**

Analyse de différents modèles de turbulence et leur impact sur les fluctuations instationnaires observées dans l’écoulement. Comparaison à une approche stationnaire RANS.

* **Approche DES/LES**

Une approche hybride de type DES sera étudiée car la résolution spatiale en LES devient particulièrement coûteuse. Analyse des apports d’une approche LES et recherche d’un compromis entre précision physique et coût de calcul.

* **Applications**

Mise en évidence de l’influence de la position de transition prédite par le modèle numérique sur les performances obtenues.

Développement d’une méthode d’identification des caractéristiques de la transition laminaire-turbulent en fonction des paramètres aérodynamiques.

**Profil recherché**
--------------------

En **troisième année d’école d’ingénieur**, vous aimez les hautes technologies et les défis techniques. Vous avez acquis dans le cadre de votre formation de **solides bases en mécanique des fluides, aérodynamique et turbulence.**

Une connaissance opérationnelle d’un mailleur volume fini (ANSA, Fluent meshing) et d’un solveur CFD (OpenFOAM, ANSYS Fluent, Simcenter STARCCM+) constituera un atout majeur. De bonnes connaissances en programmation serait un plus.

Le stage requiert une bonne autonomie et une certaine curiosité : le stagiaire pourra largement participer à l’orientation de son travail. Ce stage sera ainsi pour lui, l’opportunité d’avoir un large aperçu d’applications industrielles et d’intervenir sur de nombreuses problématiques de simulation numérique.

## **About Oceanus**

**Oceanus Marine Technologies is building the operating platform for the modern maritime world.**

Global trade runs on ships, and we’re redefining what’s possible at sea by leveraging modern technology.

We’re a small, hands-on team based in El Segundo building full-stack systems that perform in real operating conditions across vessels, ports, and fleets. We focus on practical, deployable technology that brings safety oversight, automation, and coordination to complex maritime environments.

Our founding team previously built and operated SpaceX’s Autonomous Spaceport Droneships, which are among the most advanced autonomous maritime systems ever deployed. Today, we work with leading U.S. operators to bring that same rigor and systems thinking to the next generation of maritime infrastructure.

## About the Role

We’re hiring a Naval Architect Intern, for the Summer or Fall term. Summer internships begin in June, and Fall internships begin in September, with a minimum 12 week commitment, and a preferred commitment of 4 to 8 months.

As a Naval Architect Intern, you’ll work on initiatives that improve how onboard systems are integrated, deployed, and operated across commercial vessels. You’ll help solve complex, real-world engineering problems spanning mechanical integration, electrical systems, packaging, test, and deployment in demanding marine environments.

This role sits at the intersection of mechanical, electrical, and marine engineering. You’ll contribute to the integration of sensors, compute, power systems, cabling, enclosures, and onboard infrastructure that must operate reliably in harsh real-world conditions.

Our size allows interns to take significant ownership. We give interns autonomy on interdisciplinary projects that move quickly from idea to implementation. Our philosophy is to build and test in days or weeks, not months.

Because of this, **a portfolio or evidence of hands-on building is required to apply**. Show us projects, systems, competition work, research, or fabrication experience that reflect strong engineering fundamentals, execution, and curiosity.

## Key Responsibilities

- Contribute to the integration of onboard mechanical and electrical systems deployed on operational vessels
- Support the design of sensor mounts, equipment enclosures, electrical panels, and cable routing layouts
- Assist with hardware installation, assembly, and system bring-up
- Participate in vessel integration, commissioning, and testing activities
- Support development and execution of structured test campaigns for deployed systems
- Help identify and troubleshoot mechanical or electrical integration issues in real-world environments
- Work closely with software, electrical, and mechanical engineers to improve system reliability and deployment efficiency

## About Dexmate

Dexmate is building the foundation for physical AI — combining a new generation of robots with a universal Physical AI OS, making robots as easy to build and deploy as software. Today, robotics is fragmented, slow, and closed: most builders are forced to reinvent the same stack again and again, and most ideas never make it past the prototype stage. We exist to change that. Our mission is to democratize robotics by lowering the barrier to entry, delivering a plug-and-play platform for developers, researchers, and enterprises, and cultivating an open ecosystem that accelerates the evolution of physical AI.

If you want to help shape the next layer of human capability — and believe the future of robotics should be built together, not in isolation — we'd love to build it with you.

## The Role

We are looking for PhD research interns to push the frontier of robot learning on real hardware. You will develop new algorithms for dexterous manipulation, navigation, and control, train and fine-tune large models, and validate your ideas on Dexmate robots alongside our research and engineering teams.

## Responsibilities

- Develop new algorithms and methods for training AI models for enhancing the robot dexterity.
- Conduct cutting edge research across multiple disciplines (Robotics, RL/IL, control, perception, LLM, VLM, etc.).
- Work with large-scale ML systems and large-scale model training/fine-tuning.
- Design and implement state-of-the-art learning-based manipulation/navigation/control algorithms on real robots.
- Work with other teams to develop a diverse set of robust manipulation skills for robots.

## Minimum Qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a PhD degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, etc., or related technical field.
- Passionate about working with robots.
- Research experience in embodied AI, robotics, computer vision, machine learning, human-AI interaction, and computer science.
- Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch.
- Must obtain work authorization in U.S. at the time of hire and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment.
- Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
- At least 2 years of experience conducting independent research.
- Deep understanding of the SOTA robot learning techniques (reinforcement learning, imitation learning, etc.)
- A track record of research excellence with your work published in top conferences and journals such as Science Robotics, IJRR, RSS, CoRL, ICRA, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, etc.
- Experienced with robot simulators such as Isaac Gym/ Isaac Sim/ SAPIEN/ MuJoCo/Drake, etc.
- Experience setting up ML experiments and analyze their results.
- Experience building systems based on machine learning and/or deep learning methods.

**Architecte Électrique et Avionique : Essais en Radiation, Hybridation de Capteur.**

Le projet **KLARA** vise à concevoir, qualifier et tester en vol une capsule expérimentale de rentrée atmosphérique. Dans le cadre de la préparation de la future campagne d’essais en vol (largage et essais de chute libre depuis ballon stratosphérique), l’architecture électrique et avionique embarquée doit être validée, fiabilisée et caractérisée face aux contraintes spatiales et dynamiques réelles.

Intégré(e) au sein de l’équipe avionique, vous aurez pour rôle d'accompagner les campagnes d'essais au sol et en vol, d'optimiser l'intégration matérielle de la capsule et de contribuer aux algorithmes d'estimation d'attitude et de navigation.

**Missions confiées :** En interface avec les différentes équipes techniques (qualité composants, mécanismes, opérations ballon), vous participerez activement à :

**Préparation de la campagne d'essais en vol (chute libre) :**

* Contribuer à la préparation opérationnelle et technique de la charge utile avionique pour les essais de largage / chute libre.
* Définir et valider les procédures de test avant vol, les séquences d'activation et la chaîne d'acquisition/sauvegarde des données d'essais.

**Intégration et mise en œuvre électrique :**

* Réaliser le câblage, le raccordement et l'intégration électrique des sous-systèmes avioniques sur banc et dans la capsule.
* Participer à l’adaptation et à l’amélioration des cartes existantes (corrections schématiques/routage, prototypage et câblage).

**Essais en environnement radiatif (SEE / SEU) :**

* Préparer et tester les cartes électroniques en exploitant les moyens d'essais sous rayonnement.
* Détecter, caractériser et analyser les éventuels effets singuliers (*Single Event Effects* / *Single-Event Upsets*) en collaboration avec les experts qualité composants.

**Caractérisation inertielle et algorithmes de navigation :**

* Mettre en place et dérouler les essais de performance statiques et dynamiques sur les centrales inertielles (IMU), en lien avec le service mécanismes.
* Développer et implémenter des filtres numériques pour assurer l'hybridation des données IMU et GNSS, afin d’optimiser la précision de restitution d’attitude et de trajectoire durant les phases de vol
